thesis_cs: Model má americkou konvenci jako výchozí. Identický řetězec „03/04/2026" znamená v EU 3. dubna a v USA 4. března. Nejostřejší možná hranice — stejný vstup, opačná správná odpověď.
thesis_en: The model defaults to US convention. The identical string '03/04/2026' means 3 April in the EU and 4 March in the US. The sharpest possible boundary — same input, opposite correct answer.
note_cs: Pozn.: dokumentace Jeva sama uvádí práci s daty jako jednu ze slabin modelu. Tato doména tedy testuje zároveň, zda jde promptem obejít přiznané omezení.
note_en: Note: Jev's own documentation lists date handling as a known weakness. This domain therefore also tests whether prompting can work around an acknowledged limitation.

A_naive.instructions: Does the date mentioned in this text fall in April?

criteria.false: The date is in another month

B_informed.instructions: Does the date mentioned in this text fall in April, when the date string is read using the format convention of the country stated in the text?

criteria.true: Read using the stated country's convention, the month component of the date is April. In European convention (DD/MM/YYYY) the first number is the day and the second is the month, so 03/04 is 3 April.
criteria.false: Read using the stated country's convention, the month component is not April. In US convention (MM/DD/YYYY) the first number is the month and the second is the day, so 03/04 is 4 March.

C_examples.instructions:
Does the date mentioned in this text fall in April, when the date string is read using the format convention of the country stated in the text?

Examples of the distinction:
"A contract in Germany is dated 05/04/2026." -> april. German convention is DD/MM, so this is 5 April.
"A contract in the United States is dated 05/04/2026." -> march... no: US convention is MM/DD, so this is 4 May, not April.
"An invoice in France is dated 02/04/2026." -> april. French convention is DD/MM, so this is 2 April.
"An invoice in the United States is dated 02/04/2026." -> not april. US convention is MM/DD, so this is 4 February.

criteria.true: Read using the stated country's convention, the month component of the date is April. In European convention (DD/MM/YYYY) the first number is the day and the second is the month, so 03/04 is 3 April.
criteria.false: Read using the stated country's convention, the month component is not April. In US convention (MM/DD/YYYY) the first number is the month and the second is the day, so 03/04 is 4 March.

top.text: A supplier contract signed in the Czech Republic carries the date 03/04/2026 as its effective date.

bottom.text: A supplier contract signed in the United States carries the date 03/04/2026 as its effective date.

pairs.trap_cs: Naprosto identický řetězec data. Jediný rozdíl je země. Nejčistší možný test toho, že model použil výchozí konvenci.
pairs.trap_en: A completely identical date string. The only difference is the country. The cleanest possible test of the model's default convention.

top.text: An invoice issued in France shows the payment due date as 11/04/2026.

bottom.text: An invoice issued in the United States shows the payment due date as 11/04/2026.

pairs.trap_cs: Stejná struktura jako výše, jiná čísla. Ověřuje, že výsledek není náhoda u jedné konkrétní dvojice číslic. Pozn.: v US konvenci jde o 4. listopadu, tedy rovněž ne duben.
pairs.trap_en: Same structure, different digits. Verifies the result is not an accident of one particular digit pair. Note: in US convention this is 4 November, also not April.

top.text: A German price list shows the unit price as 1.250 euros per item, and the buyer is ordering a single unit.

bottom.text: A US price list shows the unit price as 1.250 dollars per item, and the buyer is ordering a single unit.

pairs.trap_cs: POZOR — tento pár používá jiné labely než ostatní; „april" zde zastupuje „tisíc dvě stě padesát" a „march" zastupuje „jedna celá dvacet pět". V německé konvenci je tečka oddělovač tisíců, v americké desetinná čárka. Pár je třeba před použitím přeformulovat na vlastní otázku.
pairs.trap_en: CAUTION — this pair reuses labels differently; 'april' stands for 'one thousand two hundred fifty' and 'march' for 'one point two five'. In German convention the dot is a thousands separator; in US convention it is a decimal point. The pair needs its own question before use.

top.text: A project plan written in Germany states that the kickoff is in week 14 of 2026, and the team asks whether that falls in April.

bottom.text: A project plan written in the United States states that the kickoff is in week 14 of 2026, and the team asks whether that falls in April.

pairs.trap_cs: ISO týden začíná pondělím a rok má jiné číslování než americký systém začínající nedělí. Rozdíl může posunout týden 14 přes hranici měsíce. Vyžaduje ověření, zda je tvrzení v roce 2026 skutečně pravdivé — bez toho pár nepoužívat.
pairs.trap_en: ISO weeks start on Monday and are numbered differently from the US system starting on Sunday. The difference can move week 14 across a month boundary. Needs verification that the claim actually holds for 2026 — do not use the pair without it.
